Festivals · November · Oti

Ovazu

The Akposo harvest thanksgiving

Ovazu is the main harvest festival of the Akposo people of the Biakoye District in the Oti Region. It gives thanks for the fonio crop, called ova, to Uwolowu, the Almighty God, and to the seven principal Akposo gods. It is held at the harvest, between October and December.

When
At the fonio harvest, October to December
Where
Akposo towns of the Biakoye District, including Akposokubi, Kabo, Oklabe, Alifi, Obeve and Okanease
Kept by
The Akposo
The crop
Fonio (ova)
Region
Oti

What it is

Ovazu gives thanks for the fonio harvest, a small grain the Akposo call ova, to Uwolowu (Ayanuva), the Almighty God, and to the seven principal Akposo gods, the greatest of them Wetu.1 It is kept in Akposokubi, Akposo Kabo, Oklabe, Alifi, Obeve (Asukawkaw), Okanease and Akloklowa.1

The Akposo also keep a yam festival by clan and family, and smaller festivals for lesser gods; each of the seven gods has its own days of worship.1

Published accounts of Ovazu are short. If you know the festival, tell us more and we’ll add it.

Good to know if you go

  • Where: the Akposo towns are in the Biakoye District. See the Oti page for places nearby.
  • Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
  • Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

Questions people ask

What is the Ovazu festival?

The main harvest festival of the Akposo people of the Oti Region, giving thanks for the fonio crop.

When is Ovazu?

At the fonio harvest, between October and December.

Sources

  1. “Oti Region: the tradition and cultural heritage of Oti Region”, National Commission on Culture.
